text:
Maya: Quick follow-up from the kernel selection RFC — I'm proposing a lightweight 'quantization handshake' contract between model loaders and kernels so we don't embed format assumptions everywhere.

Maya: Problem we're seeing: models land with FP8/INT8/INT4 variants, but kernels have a bunch of local heuristics (packed vs unpacked, scale-per-tensor vs scale-per-row, different FP8 encodings). This causes silent slow paths and extra copies.

Alec: +1. Can you sketch the handshake?

Maya: Sketch below. It's intentionally minimal: negotiated list of supported encodings, packing/alignment requirements, and a small capability flag set.

Maya: ```c
// pseudo header exchanged at model->runtime bind time
struct QuantHandshake {
  char scheme_names[8][16]; // e.g. "fp8_e4m3", "int8_sym"
  uint8_t scheme_count;
  uint8_t bitwidth; // 8, 4 etc for primary path
  uint32_t alignment_bytes; // 16/32/64
  uint8_t scale_type; // 0=tensor,1=row,2=col
  uint8_t packed_layout; // 0=none,1=packed,2=blocked
  uint8_t fallback_policy; // 0=auto-dequant,1=call-fallback-kernel,2=reject
};
```

Sasha: This is useful. A couple of immediate tradeoffs:
- If we require alignment 64 always, older models will need a copy during load.
- If we allow packed layout negotiation, kernels get faster but we add complexity to the KV cache layout.

Kai: Thinking about KV cache: any change in packed layout will break incremental decode unless we version the cache layout in the handshake and make the router aware.

Priya: For fallback_policy, we should default to "auto-dequant" for hosted to avoid outages, but for dedicated/private customers allow stricter policies.

Alec: How does this interact with compiled kernels that only know about one encoding (e.g., fp8_e4m3)? Do we require shim kernels?

Maya: Options: (1) kernel advertises exact supported encodings and the loader will provide runtime conversion if needed (copy + dequant) ; (2) provide small in-place conversion kernels that run on the device; (3) fall back to a non-quantized kernel.

Sasha: Small in-place conversion kernels (2) are attractive: they avoid host-to-device copies. But they need to be efficient and overlap with the prep stage. Also need tests for correctness across chip variants.

Maya: Proposed default strategy (hosted): advertise all encodings models may present, prefer native match, else try device in-place conversion, else host conversion, else fallback kernel.

Kai: For dedicated/private we add an admin flag to enforce "reject" fallback for data sensitivity/cost constraints.

Priya: For rollout: implement handshake in loader + one pilot kernel that supports fp8_e4m3 and int8_sym + an in-place converter for fp8->int8 and fp8->fp32. Canary 10% of traffic per model.

Alec: Test plan?

Maya: Tests:
- unit: handshake encode/decode roundtrip + mismatch cases
- integration: model load from ONNX/pt with metadata -> verify negotiated path
- perf: microbench for conversion kernels vs host copy
- regressions: ensure KV cache decode path unchanged when layout_version unchanged

Sasha: One more ABI note: include a stable "layout_version" numeric field in the handshake so we can evolve semantics without breaking older kernels. Kernels can reject unknown layout_version or advertise compatibility ranges.

Maya: Good call. I'll add layout_version to the struct.

Priya: Where do we store the negotiated handshake? In model metadata blob, runtime state, and also emit to observability (console/traces) so SRE can see how often conversions happen.

Maya: Yes — store on model binding, and console metric "quant_conversion_bytes" + histogram of conversion_latency.

runtime-bot: Note: created tracking task INF-8242 for "quant handshake - implement header + in-place converters"

Kai: Questions about memory accounting: conversions will spike peak GPU memory. We should have a temporary staging allocator and make the scheduler aware so we don't OOM other models.

Alec: Agreed. Add a conservative per-model conversion memory budget (configurable) and a preflight check during bind. If conversion exceeds budget, either reject or force streaming conversion (slower, lower memory).

Maya: I'll draft an RFC addendum with: struct, default policies per deployment mode, canary plan, tests, metrics, and memory budget suggestion. Posting later today.

Sasha: :thumbsup: Thanks. Small ask — add a short example of how model metadata (from export) should declare quant formats so model tooling teams can instrument easily.

Maya: Will do.

Priya: If anyone wants to pair on microkernel benchmarks, ping me.

Alec: Thanks all.
